key_insight: Tilted sampling shifts the goal from finding the single best action to matching the Gibbs (soft-optimal) distribution, which changes regret from first-order to squared-confidence behavior and can yield logarithmic growth in time.
engineering_relevance: This matters for entropy-regularized RL, RLHF, and reward-guided generation because it provides principled algorithms for sampling high-quality diverse outputs rather than only optimizing a hard argmax.
method: Defines sampling regret as temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence to the Gibbs target.
Develops sampling versions of UCB and Thompson sampling (UCS and TS^2).
Derives unified regret decompositions, including a Bayesian decomposition for posterior-random Gibbs distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret guarantees, including logarithmic-in-T regret at fixed temperature in standard settings and a new Bayesian sampling-regret decomposition, rather than experimental results.
watch_item: The logarithmic guarantees depend on the fixed-temperature and standard-setting assumptions, so performance may degrade or require new analysis when temperature is very small, rewards are misspecified, or posteriors are hard to compute.
paper_title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
